issue: Can the Government withhold a U.S.S.G. § 3E1.1(b) motion for the third acceptance-of-responsibility level because the defendant insisted on a pretrial suppression hearing?

sides.position: The Government may justify withholding the third-level motion because a defendant's insistence on a suppression hearing requires Government resources, which is a valid basis under § 3E1.1(b) (Eleventh Circuit precedent so holds, and Amendment 775 did not clearly overrule it).
cases: United States v. Johnson, 980 F.3d 1364 (11th Cir. 2020)

sides.position: A defendant's insistence on a suppression hearing cannot justify the Government's refusal to move for the third level. The excerpts say three circuits took this view before Amendment 775 but do not name them.
cases: United States v. Johnson, 980 F.3d 1364 (11th Cir. 2020)

quote: As to the breadth of a timeliness assessment, the circuits are not uniform as to whether the defendant's insistence on a suppression hearing can justify the Government's refusal to make a § 3E1.1(b) motion.
cite: United States v. Sanford Eugene Johnson, III, 980 F.3d 1364 (11th Cir. 2020)
